newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest milling wheat futures start correction.
newsitem.headline: Budapest milling wheat futures start correction.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices started a downward movement on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Thursday in what traders said was a natural correction after the past two weeks.
"Prices rose during the last two weeks to a level where producers started selling their new (1997) crop," said Janos Szolyka of Swap.
He added that the downward trend was not due to a lack of buyers.
Milling wheat prices dropped 370 forints per tonne for May to end at 25,260, July finished at 21,690, down 10, and August dropped 390 forints to 22,110.
The longest maturity, March 1998, which opened on Wednesday, dropped by the daily 400-forint limit to 26,100.
Feed wheat futures also finished steady to lower, except for December, which put on 100 forints to end at 22,200.
Barley prices, pulled down by milling wheat, finished lower in every position except October and December.
Maize, despite estimated surplus stocks of roughly 500,000 tonnes, rose slightly for the nearest maturities in what Szolyka said was continuing liquidation of speculative positions.
"Continuous but not frantic liquidation kept an upward pressure on old (1996) maize prices," he said.
July maize rose 190 forints per tonne to 18,000 forints.
Total grain turnover was a meagre 202.6 million forints or 460 contracts, with milling wheat accounting for 260 and feed wheat for 138 contracts.
